title: Recursive Path Walker — Core Method
description: Nested data is a tree, and the recursive walker visits every node while remembering the path that led there — a.b[2].c — so each value arrives with its address attached. The walker handles dicts, lists, and scalars uniformly, and yields rather than collecting, so even huge documents stream through constant memory. Paths use a consistent notation that doubles as a query language for later retrieval. This is the foundation every deeper traversal technique builds on. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Path Expression Evaluation — Core Method
description: A path expression like orders[*].total names many nodes at once using wildcards and filters, and the evaluator resolves it against the document in one pass. Each step — field access, index, wildcard, predicate — is applied to the current node set to produce the next. Errors name the failing step and show the node set at that point, which makes broken expressions debuggable. Path expressions turn ad-hoc nested access into a queryable, composable operation. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Depth-Limited Traversal — Core Method
description: Deeply or infinitely nested structures can exhaust a naive walker, so traversal carries a depth budget that stops descent past the limit. Nodes at the limit are reported as truncated with their path, so nothing is silently skipped. The limit is configurable per mission — shallow for overviews, deep for audits. Depth limits turn 'walk everything' from a crash risk into a controlled operation. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Cycle Guarding — Core Method
description: Object graphs can contain cycles — a node referencing its ancestor — which send naive recursion into infinite loops. The cycle guard tracks the identity of objects on the current descent path and refuses to re-enter them, reporting the cycle's location instead. Identity is by object id, not by value, so legitimately repeated values are still visited. Guarding makes traversal safe over arbitrary graphs, not just clean trees. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Path-Map Flattening — Core Method
description: Flattening converts a nested document into a flat map from path to value — 'a.b[0].c' to 2 — which tabular tools, diff engines, and indexes can consume directly. The flattening is lossless: the path notation preserves enough structure to rebuild the original nesting. Round-trip tests verify this on every document shape the archive holds. A flattened view is often the most practical way to compare, search, and store nested records. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
